subject: Post-call recap: Q4 capacity & eval plan for Cardinal.ai — usage insights + next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@cardinal.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Q4 capacity & eval plan for Cardinal.ai — usage insights + next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we can move the evaluation toward a pilot and then a Q1 expansion decision.

Key pain points you shared:
- Increasing latency for long-context summarization requests when traffic spikes (notable at peak business hours).
- Rising per-token cost for the embedding-heavy search workload; want to reduce unit cost without regressions.
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and tighter audit logs for user query traces.

Goals you outlined:
- Run a 4–6 week pilot that proves: (a) 30–50% cost reduction on embeddings+RAG for common patterns, (b) 75ms 95th percentile latency target for 1–2k rps mixed workload, and (c) auditability for retention and access logs.

Usage snapshot (from the data you shared on the call):
- Avg tokens/day: ~9.2M (search + summarization combined)
- Peak concurrency: ~1.8k concurrent requests during daily peak
- Heavy tail: 12% of requests exceed 2k tokens

Recommended evaluation path (high level):
1) Pilot scope: set up a small Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) for controlled load testing + a prefix cache for repeated queries (see attached pilot-scope-v1.pdf).
2) Instrumentation: we will enable token-level traces and the detailed latency breakdown in the Redwood Console so we can validate 95p SLOs and cost per embed.
3) Compliance: provide SOC2 evidence & audit-log exports; we can run an access-log walkthrough during kickoff.
4) Success criteria: cost delta, latency targets, and a small QA sign-off on output quality for the summarization prompts you supplied.

Proposed next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm pilot contacts (engineering + security) and the sample test dataset you want us to use.
- Approve the pilot scope document (attached) and confirm any procurement constraints (we saw a procurement template mentioned).
- Availability for a technical kickoff next week — suggested windows: Tue 10/27 (10–11am PT) or Wed 10/28 (2–3pm PT).

We attached a short usage export (cardinal-usage-report-202610.csv) and the pilot scope. I’ll follow up with a MAP and an initial timeline once you confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on the pilot.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | (415) 555-0127

Attachments referenced: pilot-scope-v1.pdf (high-level tasks and success criteria), cardinal-usage-report-202610.csv (raw usage snapshot)

From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@cardinal.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@cardinal.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Q4 capacity & eval plan for Cardinal.ai — usage insights + next steps

Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful and lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SOC2: yes, security will need the SOC2/controls package before kickoff. Can you share the SOC2 attestation and the list of evidence items?
- Latency target: 75ms 95p is our goal for the summarization flow in production; for the pilot we can accept a slightly higher 95p (target 100ms) as long as the trend shows improvement.
- Procurement: attaching the procurement-template.docx our legal team uses. We typically need a 30-day review window for SOWs and any vendor onboarding docs.

We can provide a sanitized sample dataset for the pilot. I’ll coordinate with Tom (cc’d) and send that by EOD Monday.

Preferred kickoff: Wed 10/28 2–3pm PT works for engineering.

Samantha
Samantha Cho
Head of Product Ops | Cardinal.ai
samantha.cho@cardinal.ai

Attachments: procurement-template.docx

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@cardinal.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Q4 capacity & eval plan for Cardinal.ai — usage insights + next steps

Appreciate the quick reply and the procurement template. A few concrete points ahead of the kickoff on Wed 10/28: 

Pilot logistics we’ll prepare before the kickoff:
- Pre-provisioned Dedicated pool (2x A100 equiv) with autoscale guardrails and a single test namespace.
- Instrumentation plan: token-level traces, per-route latency, and cost telemetry. We will share dashboard links during the call.
- Compliance packet: attaching SOC2 summary and list of artifacts we can provide during onboarding. (If you prefer, we can have our security PM on the kickoff.)

Pilot acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Cost: >= 30% improvement vs current per-embed + RAG baseline for the test corpus.
- Latency: 95p <= 100ms for pilot load, trending toward 75ms with tuning.
- Quality: manual QA pass on 5 canonical summarization prompts.

Action items for kickoff (please bring):
- Cardinal test dataset (sanitized) and 3–5 canonical prompts for QA.
- Procurement contact for SOW timing (Samantha noted 30-day review).
- Any non-functional requirements (data residency, retention policy) for our security PM to note.

Ben — flagged you on pricing posture for a pilot discount and whether we can commit to the Dedicated pool sizing above while we evaluate. Marissa — would you take point on the MAP once we have the kickoff notes?

I’ll attach the SOC2 summary and the MAP draft in a follow-up email so we have a version to iterate on before the kickoff. See you Wednesday 10/28 at 2pm PT.

—
Jasmine

Attachments referenced: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached in follow-up), pilot-scope-v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@cardinal.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Q4 capacity & eval plan for Cardinal.ai — usage insights + next steps

Quick note from pricing — we can offer a pilot package with a one-time credit that covers ~50% of incremental Dedicated compute for the 4–6 week evaluation (details to be drafted in the MAP). Approving this on principle so Jasmine can confirm to the customer.

Marissa — please work with Jasmine to draft the MAP and pull together the estimated pilot SOW; we should also include an optional path to a reserved capacity commitment in Q1 if the pilot meets the success criteria.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

(Internal: will loop Revenue Ops for SOW template and Finance for procurement timelines.)
